title: Scoped integrity preflight and trace relocation
objective: Stop an unrelated scope's drift from blocking work on a healthy scope, and keep trace writes out of the scope-discovery tree.
successCriteria: Every startup surface resolves the target scope before integrity prepare and passes --kyro-scope through prepare, apply, and the post-repair doctor check.
A healthy scope routes, closes, and passes scoped Doctor while an unrelated scope on disk is irreconcilable.
An explicit global scan without --kyro-scope still reports every scope.
A trace write can never create a directory that scope discovery classifies as a scope.
Trace history recorded at the previous location stays readable and merges in timestamp order.
A regression gate fails if any startup surface reintroduces a global integrity preflight.

requirements.statement: Every startup surface must resolve the target scope before running integrity prepare, and must pass --kyro-scope to it.
requirements.rationale: The preflight ran before scope resolution and without a scope, so drift in any scope blocked routing for every scope.

requirements.statement: Verification that follows a scoped repair must stay bound to the repaired scope.
requirements.rationale: A global doctor --artifacts after a successful scoped repair still let an unrelated scope's failure block the flow.

requirements.statement: A project-wide integrity scan must remain available when a human explicitly asks for it.
requirements.rationale: Isolating the routine path must not remove the ability to audit the whole project on purpose.

requirements.statement: Trace events must be written outside the tree that scope discovery scans.
requirements.rationale: A trace write for a name with no sprint.json created a directory under scopes/ that discovery then classified as an invalid scope.

requirements.statement: Trace history recorded at the previous location must stay readable and must merge with current-path events in chronological order.
requirements.rationale: Moving the path must not hide forensic history, and a rollback or mixed-version runtime can still append to the previous location after current-path events exist.

requirements.statement: Scope discovery must ignore an existing directory whose only content is a leftover trace folder.
requirements.rationale: Preventing new phantom scopes does not help installs that already carry one from the previous layout.

requirements.statement: A regression gate must fail if any startup surface reintroduces a global integrity preflight or an unscoped post-repair doctor.
requirements.rationale: The defect is one wording edit away from returning, across four separate files that must stay in agreement.

scenarios.given: a healthy scope A and an unrelated scope B on disk whose sprint.json is invalid
scenarios.when: a startup surface runs its integrity preflight for scope A
scenarios.then: the preflight reports no findings and no blockers, and routing continues for A

scenarios.given: a scoped integrity repair that has just been applied to scope A
scenarios.when: recover mode runs its post-repair verification
scenarios.then: the verification is bound to scope A and is not failed by unrelated scope B

scenarios.given: a healthy scope A and an irreconcilable scope B
scenarios.when: a human runs repair integrity prepare with no --kyro-scope
scenarios.then: the plan still reports B as a blocker

scenarios.given: a command that emits trace events for a scope
scenarios.then: they land under .agents/kyro/trace/{scope}/ and create nothing under .agents/kyro/scopes/

scenarios.given: a previous-location trace file whose newest event is later than the newest current-location event
scenarios.when: kyro trace reads the scope with a tail limit
scenarios.then: events are ordered by timestamp and the tail keeps the genuinely newest event

scenarios.given: events at both locations carrying identical timestamps
scenarios.when: kyro trace reads the scope twice
scenarios.then: both reads render the same stable order

scenarios.given: a directory under scopes/ whose only content is a leftover trace folder
scenarios.then: the directory is not reported as a scope and is not classified as irreconcilable

scenarios.given: a startup surface edited to call repair integrity prepare without --kyro-scope
scenarios.then: the gate fails and names the offending file and line

nonGoals: Adding a public command or changing the public command surface.
Changing prepareIntegrityPlan or classifyRegistry scoping logic, which already isolates correctly when given a scope.
Migrating, moving, or deleting trace files that already exist on disk.
Reopening or modifying the closed integrity-recovery scope.
Deciding or publishing the next release version.

conventions.rule: Fail closed on the operation being performed; degrade in isolation everywhere else. A project-wide scan runs only when a human explicitly asks for it, never implicitly during routing.
Tool-owned side artifacts (trace, locks, repair records) must never live under a path that discovery scans for scopes.
When a contract is duplicated across several startup assets, add a gate that fails if any copy drifts; agreement between Markdown files is not self-enforcing.

roadmap.sizingRationale: One sprint: the change is a startup-order correction across four assets plus one path relocation with read compatibility, all provable by a single new portable gate.

recommendations: Decide the next version and move the Unreleased entry into it before publishing; 4.47.0 is already on npm.
Consider promoting the scope-bound-by-default rule to a global convention via kyro rule add --global.
Audit any remaining project-wide check that runs implicitly during routing for the same blast-radius shape.

previousSprint.summary: Scope-isolated integrity preflight and trace relocation, gated against regression.

handoff.note: Follow-up to integrity-recovery: fixes the product defect that made one broken scope block every scope. No release decision taken; CHANGELOG entry sits under Unreleased.
